Rewrite the expression as
\[
\frac{\sin(6x)}{x}=6\frac{\sin(6x)}{6x}.
\]
Since \(6x\to0\), the standard sine limit gives
\[
\frac{\sin(6x)}{6x}\to1.
\]
Therefore the limit is \(6\).

Divide numerator and denominator by \(t\):
\[
\frac{\sin(2t)}{\sin(3t)}=\frac{\sin(2t)/t}{\sin(3t)/t}.
\]
Using the scaled sine limit, the numerator tends to \(2\) and the denominator tends to \(3\), so the limit is
\[
\frac{2}{3}.
\]

Use \(1-\cos u=2\sin^2(u/2)\) with \(u=2x\):
\[
1-\cos(2x)=2\sin^2 x.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{1-\cos(2x)}{x^2}=2\left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^2.
\]
The sine fraction tends to \(1\), so the limit is \(2\).
